axes.label: Fertigkeit
axes.rule: Jeder Wert schliesst den vorherigen ein. Ein hoeherer Wert ohne den geforderten Beleg faellt auf den naechstniedrigeren zurueck.

axes.label: Wirksamkeit
axes.rule: Beschreibt, ob eine Sache nur benannt ist, warnt oder blockt. Unabhaengig von der Fertigkeit.

axes.label: Umkehrbarkeit
axes.rule: Beschreibt, ob der Zustand zurueckgenommen werden kann.

mandatoryClauses.rule: Whoever reports a state names its carrier — the thing the state refers to.
mandatoryClauses.reason: A state word without a carrier cannot be checked.

mandatoryClauses.rule: From WIRED upward the evidence is named with the value. Without it, the next lower value holds.
mandatoryClauses.reason: The speaker binding comes from the duty of evidence, not from a prohibition.

mandatoryClauses.rule: When the register holds no word for the state reached, the state is reported as NOT FULLY COMPLETED and the missing word is reported.
mandatoryClauses.reason: An unnamed state invites inventing a word.

mandatoryClauses.rule: The information comes before the calibration. A state word is corrected, not negotiated.
mandatoryClauses.reason: A register that makes people talk about words instead of the state would not abolish the debating club but give it a rulebook (user correction in conversation, memo 083 revision REV-04, line 1106).

terms.label: Memo
terms.definition: A versioned strategy document and the single highest authority over its own rollout; its content is local and MUST NOT be uploaded.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a shareable or uploadable document, and NOT a cross-memo container — a memo has authority over its OWN rollout; the cross-memo span belongs to a goal or a plan.

terms.label: Revision
terms.definition: One immutable snapshot of a memo's content, stored as REV-XX.md; each change produces a new file, so the history is forward-only.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT an in-place edit — a revision is never mutated; a change is always a new REV-XX file.

terms.label: Topic
terms.definition: An atomic point extracted from the input during the five-step input pipeline; the complete topic list serves as a writing checklist and is the head of the Topic to Block to PRD chain.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT too small to omit and NOT cross-memo — extraction is exhaustive and topics are memo-scoped.

terms.label: Goal
terms.definition: A cross-memo intent (id G###) that spans several memos and outlives any one; defined by intent not surface, and scored in a fresh context against real state.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT scoped inside one memo and NOT surface-defined — a goal spans the memo sequence and is never scored in the session that did the work.

terms.label: Block
terms.definition: A structure node inside a memo carrying its own B### identifier; it references one or more topics and is the unit PRDs are derived from.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a synonym for a context block — it is an addressable structure node with a B### id, not a chunk of prose context.

terms.label: PRD
terms.definition: A block-derived chunk of work sized so one PRD fits into one context (hard cap one third, smart-zone one quarter) and is implementable by one agent in one thread.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a multi-thread or multi-context unit — if work needs a second thread, that is the signal to chunk into more PRDs, not to span one PRD across threads.

terms.label: Phase
terms.definition: A sequential, mandatory unit of the rollout that bundles PRDs executed together and in order, carrying an orchestration role and a mandatory depends-on.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT optional and NOT parallel by default — a phase is mandatory and sequential; depends-on is a required characteristic, not decoration.

terms.label: Strand
terms.definition: The emergent dependency closure over phases — the transitive closure of the depends-on edges, derived by walking the graph, never authored.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT authored and NOT a thematic bundle — a strand is emergent, and it is a tag, never part of the numeric memo ID.

terms.label: Requirement
terms.definition: A single addressable statement that must, should, or may hold; two-sided (statement faces generation, check faces the gate) with an optional grade axis, resolving to a ternary status.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT one-sided and NOT self-graded — a requirement faces both generation and the gate, a check that did not run MUST NOT report PASS, and the doer MUST NOT be the grader.

terms.label: Tool
terms.definition: An external capability a phase or PRD depends on, recorded as a descriptor in the per-project tools registry that says that a tool exists, what it is for, and where it lives.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a runtime and NOT an enforced gate — the registry is descriptive and a RECOMMENDATION; a memo MUST NOT be blocked solely because no registry is present.

terms.label: Plan
terms.definition: The execution-side primitive above the single memo: it spans one or more finalized memos and sequences their phases into a single ordered run (id PLAN-###-slug).
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a replacement for the per-memo stage model — a plan nests the four stages per carried memo; and phase order stays the memo's to decide (memo authority).

terms.label: User Role
terms.definition: The interactive role in the harness tool-contract roles{} (10-harness-registry): the surface a developer drives directly; it adds the interaction tool to core.required[] and is the top-level trust reference the other two roles are bounded under.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT the same as a 'User session' type — the role is the tool-contract delta in roles.user, while the session type is the session-tier classification that anchors trust; and NOT a self-granted privilege.

terms.label: Orchestrator Role
terms.definition: The coordinating role in the harness tool-contract roles{} (10-harness-registry): it adds the coordination tools to core.required[] and carries the gate-dependent taskCrud marker; it runs work on the user's behalf and MUST NOT exceed the user's trust level.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a new authority — the orchestrator is the user's context continued into coordination, bounded by monotonicity, never a separate higher privilege; and NOT the lead role (governance 05-roles), which is a role of its own that runs under this contract role.

terms.label: Lead Role
terms.definition: The role (governance 05-roles) that may create worker sub-agents, and only with fewer rights than it holds itself; it communicates only with the orchestrator and runs under the orchestrator contract role.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT the orchestrator role — a lead never talks to the user and never ascends to the orchestrator; and NOT a worker — a worker creates no sub-agents, a lead does.

terms.label: Worker Role
terms.definition: The scoped-execution role in the harness tool-contract roles{} (10-harness-registry): it adds structured-output and removes the coordination tools, executing one bounded unit of work in an isolated context.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT an orchestrator — a worker cannot coordinate a team or spawn one; and NOT a persistent identity — a worker is a scoped, one-unit execution, bounded below the orchestrator that started it.

terms.label: Contamination
terms.definition: The umbrella condition of a context taking on content that mis-weights the output; a document written out of such a rotten context carries the mis-weighting forward. The common case is unconscious self-contamination, where the working context silently loads non-instruction material that then steers the result.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a synonym for prompt injection — prompt injection (externally, maliciously supplied instructions) is the malicious special case, one bounded subtype; the general rule is unconscious self-contamination, not an outside attacker. And NOT the same as context rot, which is the cause (quality decay as input length grows) while contamination is the effect.

terms.label: Trajectory
terms.definition: The runtime action-history a session actually produced — the recorded, ordered sequence of steps, agent spawns, and tool calls a running context walked over its session-and-subagent tree, so a result can be traced backward to the step that produced it. It is the concept the session tree operationalizes.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a Strand — a strand is the computed dependency-closure structure over phases, derived by walking the depends-on graph and never authored; a trajectory is the runtime action-history that was actually traversed, recorded not computed. And NOT a plan: a plan sequences intended work forward, a trajectory records executed work as it happened.

terms.label: Back Pressure
terms.definition: The requirements practice seen from the generation side: in-scope requirement statements are surfaced before the work is done, constraining the doer up front, as the complement of the gate that checks the work afterward.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT infrastructure flow-control (queue throttling, rate limiting, TCP back-pressure) — it is the requirements-as-constraint discipline that pushes back on generation, not a runtime traffic mechanism.

terms.label: Inner Harness
terms.definition: The surface the agent harness itself exposes and the org does not control — the tool definitions, the agent/skill/task mechanics, and the versioned config surface a harness carries; the given layer, captured by the harness descriptor.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT the layer the org builds; the inner harness is the given, non-modifiable surface. And NOT the harness descriptor itself — the descriptor is the record OF the inner harness, not the harness.

terms.label: Outer Harness
terms.definition: Everything the org builds around the given inner harness — the standing rules and hooks, the local memo convention, the viewer and its channels; the layer the org owns, shapes, and maintains on top of the harness.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT the given inner surface the harness exposes; the outer harness is the org-built layer, never the harness's own tool or config surface. And NOT a second harness process — it is the project layer running inside one harness invocation.

terms.label: SOP
terms.definition: A namespace's canonical entry document and read-gate: the minimal signpost a reader must load first, that names where other information lives and in what order the guardrails apply. It classifies every skill in its scope as either a public entry point or a private process step.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a container of all rules (it points, it does not hoard); NOT a public skill; NOT the process it delegates to.

terms.label: Register
terms.definition: How something is written for its audience — the composed choice of direction (inward/outward), language (one per artifact), and formality (formal vs. working, NR1/NR2). A property of the written artifact, chosen deliberately per artifact.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT locality (where the bytes live); NOT secrecy (the test is direction, not what is hidden).

terms.label: Tier
terms.definition: The structural level a skill or rule lives on: sop (the namespace signpost), public (a validated entry point), or private (an internal process step). The tier decides the template a skill follows and how it is disclosed.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT the GEE role (generate/execute/evaluate/orchestrate, an orthogonal axis); NOT visibility alone.

terms.label: Evidence
terms.definition: The backing recorded for a substantive statement: exactly one of the six ordered level tags, assigned inline, naming how strongly the statement is supported and what would confirm it.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT the statement itself and NOT the source the statement cites — evidence is the graded backing attached to a claim, not the claim and not its reference. The machine token is the field name `evidence`; a rendered display label in the project working language is that same field shown to a reader, NOT a second term.

terms.label: OPEN
terms.definition: The work on this carrier has not started. No artifact exists for it yet.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a state that carries any partial result — the moment a first artifact exists the value is IN PROGRESS.

terms.label: IN PROGRESS
terms.definition: Work on this carrier has started and a partial artifact exists. The artifact does not yet do what it is for.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a claim that anything works — it states only that work began.

terms.label: BUILT
terms.definition: The artifact exists and is internally finished, but nothing calls it and no gate enforces it. It does not act on the system.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a claim of effect. An artifact that exists but has no caller is BUILT, never WIRED and never COMPLETED. This is the value that the sentence "I have implemented it" MUST resolve to.

terms.label: WIRED
terms.definition: The artifact is reached by a named caller on a call path that was followed from a fresh context. The caller MUST be named with the evidence.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a claim that the artifact is enforced — an artifact can be reached and still only report. Effectiveness is the separate axis. Without a named caller the value falls back to BUILT.

terms.label: COMPLETED
terms.definition: Successfully brought to an end, confirmed by a check that the reporter did not run. The check and its comparison count MUST be named with the evidence.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT sayable by the instance that did the work — a builder has no independent evidence and therefore cannot reach this value. A state value read out of a generate-state file is not evidence of finished work.

terms.label: NAMED
terms.definition: The rule or gate exists in writing and is findable, but it does not act on any run.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a degree of enforcement — it is the absence of enforcement with a written carrier.

terms.label: ARMED-WARNS
terms.definition: The gate runs on every relevant event and reports a finding. It does not stop the run. The event that triggers it MUST be named.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a block. A warning that is dismissed by habit has the effect of NAMED, and its false-positive rate belongs to the evidence.

terms.label: ARMED-BLOCKS
terms.definition: The gate runs on every relevant event and stops the run on a finding. The event and the exit behaviour MUST be named.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT to be used where a fallback swallows the failure. A path that ends in a tolerated failure is ARMED-WARNS at most.

terms.label: REVERSIBLE
terms.definition: The state can be taken back by a named operation without loss.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a judgement about difficulty — it states that a take-back path exists and is named.

terms.label: FINAL
terms.definition: The state cannot be taken back. A push, a publication and a deletion outside the trash are final.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT the same as COMPLETED — a state can be final and still not finished.

terms.label: MAKE SURE
terms.definition: The single approved verb for a check. It names what was compared and how many items the comparison covered.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT a scale. The thirteen measured variants imply a hardness ranking that nobody defined and that lets a reporter claim rigour it did not spend. ENSURE is refused in particular because it grammatically asserts the result instead of the action.

terms.label: Health
terms.definition: The state in which a project, the setup of its workbench and its test suite are in working order, as answered by the scripts of the health family in the scripts/ folder of a project — a deterministic check with an exit code, not a judgement.
terms.negativeDelimitation: NOT the maintenance score of a repository and NOT the liveness probe of a running service; a health script verifies a setup, it neither grades quality nor keeps a service alive.
